role_in_parent: Show that on each early interval, the maximum is attained at the left endpoint m/n.
statement_nl: For every integer m with 0 <= m <= n-2, the function F_n is nonincreasing on the interval [m/n, (m+1)/n): if x and y lie in this interval and x <= y, then F_n(y) <= F_n(x).

domain_restrictions: the comparisons F_n(y) <= F_n(x) are meaningful, so outputs of F_n are in an orderable domain
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Fix an integer n. For every integer m with 0 <= m <= n-2, and for all real numbers x and y in [m/n, (m+1)/n) with x <= y, the inequality F_n(y) <= F_n(x) holds.
quantifier_order: for every integer m such that 0 <= m <= n-2
for all real numbers x and y such that x and y lie in [m/n, (m+1)/n) and x <= y

variables.name: n
variables.role: global parameter indexing the function F_n and the partition size

variables.name: x
variables.role: left argument point in the subinterval

variables.name: y
variables.role: right argument point in the subinterval

variables.domain: at least defined on every real number in the union of intervals [m/n, (m+1)/n) for allowed m
variables.name: F_n
variables.role: maps inputs x to outputs F_n(x) that can be compared with <= (belonging to a totally ordered set)

witness_dependencies: No existential witnesses are introduced; the universal conditions quantify x and y directly within the same chosen interval determined by m
